paragraphs: The S580 is the flagship V8 variant of the W223-generation S-Class, introduced in 2021 as a replacement for the S560. For its first four years of production (2021 to 2025), it used the M176 — a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with mild-hybrid assistance, the same engine family used in the preceding S560 and Maybach S580. From the 2026 model-year facelift, Mercedes introduced a running change to the M177 Evo, a more powerful 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with a flat-plane crank and revised hybrid system. The exact production changeover date hasn't been confirmed yet, so if your S580 is a 2026 model or later, we'll confirm which engine you have by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S580 on the road.

cards.body: A 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 with mild-hybrid assistance, fitted to the S580 from the W223's launch in 2021 until the 2025 model-year. A proven, powerful V8 shared with the Maybach S580 and GLS 580.

compatibility.intro: Because the S580 spans two distinct V8 engines across a single generation, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M176 part will work on an M177 Evo car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
